title: Quadratic Equations

source.syllabus: NTA, Syllabus for JEE (Main) 2026, Paper 1 Mathematics, Unit 2: quadratic equations in real and complex number systems and their solutions; relations between roots and coefficients; nature of roots; formation of quadratic equations with given roots.
source.marking: NTA, Information Bulletin JEE (Main) 2026: Section A multiple choice and Section B numerical value, +4 correct, -1 incorrect, 0 unanswered; numerical answers are integers.

cards.title: The standard form
cards.text: A quadratic equation is ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. It always has two roots, α and β, in the complex numbers (they may be equal).

cards.title: The formula
cards.text: α, β = (−b ± √D) / 2a, where D = b² − 4ac is the discriminant.

cards.title: Nature of roots
cards.text: D > 0: two different real roots. D = 0: two equal real roots. D < 0: two non-real roots, complex conjugates p ± qi (for real a, b, c).

cards.title: Sum and product
cards.text: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a. You can often answer without finding α and β at all.

cards.title: Useful identities
cards.text: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ.   α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β).   (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ.

cards.title: Building an equation
cards.text: With roots α and β: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0. Multiply through to clear fractions.

stages.title: Worked example
stages.problem: α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 1 = 0. Find α³ + β³.
steps: Do not solve for α and β. Read the sum and product from the coefficients: a = 1, b = −4, c = 1.
Answer: 52. A numerical-value question would want the integer 52, and the same idea works for α² + β², 1/α + 1/β and α⁴ + β⁴.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0. Find α² + β².
questions.hint: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6. Use α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ.

questions.solution: D = (−4)² − 4 × 2 × 5 = 16 − 40 = −24 < 0, so the roots are non-real complex conjugates. (With real coefficients, non-real roots always come in a conjugate pair, so D is never 'one real, one non-real'.)

questions.prompt: For k > 0, x² + kx + 16 = 0 has equal roots. Find k.
The quadratic equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 − √3 is:
questions.hint: Find the sum and the product of the two roots.
questions.solution: Sum = 4, product = (2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 4 − 3 = 1. The equation is x² − 4x + 1 = 0.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0. Find α³ + β³.
questions.hint: α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β), with α + β = 3 and αβ = 1.

questions.prompt: The roots of x² − (k + 1)x + k = 0 differ by 3, and k > 1. Then k equals:
questions.hint: Try x = 1 in the equation. Then the other root is the product divided by 1.
questions.solution: x = 1 is a root (1 − k − 1 + k = 0), so the other root is k (the product). k − 1 = 3 gives k = 4.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² + 4x − 5 = 0. Find |α − β|.
The roots of x² − 2kx + 9 = 0 are real exactly when:
questions.solution: D = 4k² − 36 ≥ 0 gives k² ≥ 9, that is |k| ≥ 3 (k ≤ −3 also works).

The number of real roots of x² − 5|x| + 6 = 0 is:
questions.solution: Let t = |x| ≥ 0: t² − 5t + 6 = 0 gives t = 2 or 3, so x = ±2, ±3: four real roots.

questions.prompt: x² + 2(k − 1)x + (k + 5) = 0 has equal roots. The sum of all possible values of k is:
questions.solution: D = 4(k − 1)² − 4(k + 5) = 0 gives k² − 3k − 4 = 0, so k = 4 or k = −1. Their sum is 3.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − x − 1 = 0. Find α⁴ + β⁴. (Numerical value: enter an integer.)
questions.solution: α² + β² = 1 + 2 = 3. Then α⁴ + β⁴ = (α² + β²)² − 2(αβ)² = 9 − 2 = 7.
